answer: One defense is to forge identities slowly: the network issues new identities only at a capped rate from a periodic lottery, so a farm cannot mint ten thousand personas in an afternoon. Fresh identities start in a lagoon — a quarantined sandbox where they trade only with other newcomers under tight limits — and climb onto the open mesa of the full economy only after earning attestations from diverse, established peers. Each lottery entry burns a small fee, and the fee pool funds bounties paid to anyone who proves two identities share an operator, so the attacker's own scale pays the hunters.
